test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 15 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a marine fish?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rohu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rohu** (**Labeo rohita**) is a species of fish of the **carp family** (**Cyprinidae**) found in **freshwater** rivers in **South Asia**.
 
• It is a large **omnivore** and is used extensively in **aquaculture** in countries like **India**, **Bangladesh**, **Nepal**, and **Pakistan**. ***Hence, it is not a marine fish.***
 
• It belongs to the category of **Indian Major Carps**, which also includes other freshwater species like **Catla** and **Mrigal**.
 
• **Pomfret** is a **marine fish** found in the **Indo-Pacific** region and is widely consumed in the coastal regions of **India**. ***Hence, statement 1 describes a marine fish.***
 
• **Mackerel** is a common name applied to a number of different species of **pelagic marine fish**, mostly from the family **Scombridae**. ***Hence, statement 4 describes a marine fish.***
 
• **Bhetki**, also known as **Barramundi**, is a **euryhaline** species (can tolerate various salinities) but is primarily found in **estuaries**, **backwaters**, and **marine** coastal waters. ***Hence, it is considered a marine/estuarine fish.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Marine Fisheries:**

 
 
• These involve the exploitation of fish resources from **saltwater** bodies such as **oceans** and **seas**.
 
• In **India**, the marine fishery resources are spread along the **8,118 km** long coastline.
 
• Important marine fish varieties include **Hilsa**, **Sardines**, **Tuna**, **Mackerel**, and **Pomfret**.
 
• The **exclusive economic zone (EEZ)** of India provides a vast area for **deep-sea fishing** operations.
 
 
 
• **Inland Fisheries:**
 
 
• This refers to the catching and farming of fish in **freshwater** resources like **canals**, **ponds**, **reservoirs**, and **rivers**.
 
• **Rohu** is the most important among the **three Indian major carp** species used in polyculture systems.
 
• **Freshwater aquaculture** contributes to a significant portion of the total fish production in **India**, with states like **Andhra Pradesh** and **West Bengal** leading the sector.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Rohu:**
 
 
• **Age and Growth:** It can reach a **maximum length** of about **2 meters** and can live for several years under optimal conditions.
 
• **Features:** It has **cycloid scales**, a **depressed snout**, and is typically **bluish-grey** or **black** on the back with a **silvery-white** belly.
 
• **Diet:** It is mainly a **column feeder**, consuming **phytoplankton** and **decaying organic matter**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Distinction based on Salinity:**

 
 
• **Marine fish** are adapted to high **salinity** levels and possess specialized **osmoregulation** mechanisms to prevent dehydration.
 
• **Freshwater fish** like **Rohu** are adapted to low-salinity environments; placing them in **seawater** would lead to fatal **osmotic shock**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The **Blue Revolution** in **India** aimed to increase fish production and productivity from both **marine** and **inland** sources.
 
• **Mackerel** and **Pomfret** are high-value **export** items, contributing significantly to India's **foreign exchange** earnings.
 
• **Rohu** remains the primary source of **animal protein** for a large section of the population in **North** and **East India**.
